subject: Clarification: sidecar proxy chaining, KV cache boundaries & threat scenarios (RFI)
content:
From: Alice Chen <alice.chen@meridianbank.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 01 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Questions on sidecar proxy chaining & KV cache isolation

Hi Marcus / Vanessa,

Thanks for the topology doc in the RFP — a couple of follow-ups from our security/architecture team as we map to our network and audit requirements:

1) Sidecar chaining: can Redwood sidecar proxies be chained across multiple network hops (for example: customer tenant -> regional gateway -> central inspection proxy)? If yes, how do you preserve tenant binding and prevent request replay or cross-tenant header contamination when a proxy drops or restarts?

2) KV cache scoping: we rely on cached KV/state for performance. How is the KV cache scoped per-tenant and per-model-version? What are the eviction/invalidation signals and how would you prove no cross-tenant leakage in an audit?

3) Egress and fallback behavior: if a preferred egress (private peering) fails, what fallback paths do you use and how are those failovers logged and authenticated?

4) Threat scenarios: we need a short list (3-4) of credible attack paths against the proxy/cache surface and the mitigations you supply. A simple diagram and short threat-summary would be ideal.

Can you send a short write-up + diagram we can include in our security pack? We have a short timeline (decision window next week).

Best,
Alice Chen
Senior Infrastructure Security Engineer
Meridian Bank

——— reply ———

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Alice Chen <alice.chen@meridianbank.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 01 Dec 2026 12:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Questions on sidecar proxy chaining & KV cache isolation

Alice — thanks for the concrete questions. Attaching a short topology and a KV cache flow image that address each point. Summary below; attachments: redwood_sidecar_topology_v2.pdf, kv_cache_flow.png.

Quick summary answers:
- Sidecar chaining: supported but explicit tenant binding is enforced at each hop via signed request headers and an HMAC envelope on the per-request metadata. If a proxy restarts, the HMAC validation prevents header replay — the runtime rejects any request with a mismatched sequence token.
- KV cache scoping: caches are namespaced by (customer_id, model_id, model_version, routing_shard). In-memory caches are ephemeral to the process; persistent cache shards (optional) are explicitly provisioned per-customer. Cache invalidation signals: model rollout hooks, explicit admin eviction APIs, and TTL-based eviction.
- Egress fallback: primary path is private peering; fallback order is (1) regional private egress to customer VPC, (2) encrypted public egress via dedicated NAT with ephemeral source attestations, (3) queued delivery to a customer pull endpoint. All failovers are logged with correlation ids and signed attestations.

Suggested next step: 20–30 minute call with our security architect (Mina) to walk the diagrams and produce a short threat-summary artifact for your pack. Available windows: Wed 10–11am PT or Thu 2–4pm PT.

Thanks,
Marcus Lin
Head of Infrastructure Security
Redwood Inference
Attachment: redwood_sidecar_topology_v2.pdf (diagram, 2 pages)
Attachment: kv_cache_flow.png (flowchart)

——— reply ———

From: Rajiv Nair <rajiv.nair@meridianbank.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Alice Chen <alice.chen@meridianbank.com>
Date: Wed, 02 Dec 2026 10:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Questions on sidecar proxy chaining & KV cache isolation

Marcus / Team — thanks for the quick response. A couple of clarifying points before the call:

- You mention HMAC envelope and sequence tokens — where are those sequence tokens stored and how are they rotated? If a regional proxy is compromised, can it mint tokens for subsequent requests?

- For persistent cache shards: do you support customer-managed persistent cache (i.e., an optional sidecar that keeps cache on customer storage) vs Redwood-managed? Does the audit trail show which cache shard served a response (useful for incident reconstruction)?

- For the fallback egress path that uses ephemeral source attestations — can you provide an example of the attestation format and the log record we would receive? We need to validate the log format for our SIEM ingestion.

Also: we would like a short, prioritized list of mitigations per attack path (e.g., detect, prevent, respond).

Thanks,
Rajiv
Principal Cloud Architect
Meridian Bank

——— reply ———

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Rajiv Nair <rajiv.nair@meridianbank.com>
Cc: Alice Chen <alice.chen@meridianbank.com>, Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 03 Dec 2026 16:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Questions on sidecar proxy chaining & KV cache isolation

Rajiv / Alice — thanks, good follow-ups. Below is a concise technical response and a 3-scenario threat summary (we'll include the detailed diagram pages in the attached PDF). If helpful we'll convert this into a 1-page appendix you can drop into your pack.

1) Sequence tokens & HMAC envelope
- Where stored: sequence tokens are ephemeral monotonic counters with short-term lease metadata stored in an internal, strongly-consistent cache (not persisted to disk) per-proxy instance. The HMAC input is (tenant_id + request_id + sequence_token + timestamp). HMAC keys are rotated monthly and provisioned via KMS; each sidecar fetches the active key via mTLS from the control plane and caches the key in memory with a short TTL.
- Compromise scenario: if a regional proxy is compromised, its ability to mint valid HMACs is limited by the key material and sequence window. We mitigate by: (a) short sequence windows (seconds), (b) anomaly detection on sequence gaps at the next hop, and (c) attestation checks — remote hops request proof-of-origin from the control plane when sequence patterns diverge. Compromise recovery includes revocation of the proxy lease and key rotation; all affected sequence tokens are invalidated.

2) Persistent cache options & audit trail
- Modes supported: (A) Redwood-managed ephemeral in-process caches (default); (B) Redwood-managed persistent cache shards (optional, per-tenant); (C) Customer-managed persistent cache via a dedicated sidecar that stores to customer-controlled storage (S3/GCS) and exposes a restricted API.
- Auditability: every cache hit includes a cache_shard_id header in the response metadata. Redis-like shards include a signed shard id and timestamp. Our access logs capture (request_id, shard_id, hit/miss, model_version, correlation_id). We can provide a sample CSV log format for SIEM ingestion.

3) Egress attestations & log format
- Attestation example (high level): {attestation_version:1, correlation_id:UUID, chosen_path:PEERING|REGIONAL_NAT|QUEUED_PULL, egress_ip:, signed_by:REDWOOD-EDGE, signature:BASE64}.
- Example log record (CSV friendly): timestamp, correlation_id, tenant_id, chosen_path, egress_ip, attestation_signature, reason_code. We will provide a JSON schema + a 1-line example you can ingest into SIEM. Link included in the related_links above.

4) Prioritized threat scenarios (3)
- Scenario A — Cross-tenant KV leakage via cache key collision:
  - Attack: malformed requests attempt to force key collisions across namespace boundaries in a misconfigured cache.
  - Mitigations: strict namespacing (tenant_id + model_version enforced in the cache key), signed cache_shard_id on responses, and cache key randomization for persistent shards. Detection: spike in cache shard hits across tenant_id anomaly detection rule. Response: automatic shard quarantine, key rotation, forensics export.

- Scenario B — Proxy chain header replay & request spoofing:
  - Attack: compromised middle proxy attempts to replay previously seen requests or inject headers to escalate access.
  - Mitigations: HMAC envelope + sequence tokens, mTLS between proxies, control-plane attestation checks and per-hop nonce verification. Detection: sequence window anomalies + mismatch between control-plane expected leases and observed sequences. Response: immediate lease revocation, route blackhole, and forced restart with new keys.

- Scenario C — Egress traffic exfil via fallback public egress:
  - Attack: attacker deliberately causes peering failure then monitors fallback path to siphon data.
  - Mitigations: ephemeral source attestations, strict egress ACLs, per-request encryption with customer-provided keys (optional), and destination allow-lists. Detection: correlation_id drift + unexpected destination IPs. Response: failover rollback, SIEM alerting, and forensic packet capture if requested under NDA.

Artifacts we will provide for your security pack:
- redwood_sidecar_topology_v2.pdf (deployment zones, per-hop authentication, and failover flow)
- kv_cache_flow.png (namespacing and eviction diagrams)
- meridian_attack_scenarios.docx (short threat-summary appendix with sample logs)

Next steps: Mina (cc'd) can run the 20–30 minute walkthrough and we will prepare the 1-page appendix and a sample CSV log snippet for SIEM. Proposed times (again): Thu 2pm PT or Fri 9am PT. Let us know which works and we’ll send a calendar invite + Zoom link.

Thanks,
Marcus Lin
Head of Infrastructure Security
Redwood Inference

On behalf of the Security Architecture team
Attachment: meridian_attack_scenarios.docx (3 pages, threat summary + sample logs)
